newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba refrains from condemning Peru embassy attack.
newsitem.headline: Cuba refrains from condemning Peru embassy attack.

text.p: Cuba, which has two diplomats among the hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, said on Thursday it was following the case closely but refrained from condemning the attack.

Its caution appeared to be a response to foreign media speculation that Cuba might be asked to help mediate with the leftist guerrillas, said to be Cuban inspired, who stormed the residence on Tuesday night. But a Foreign Ministry spokesman declined to comment on any possible mediation.

Spokesman Miguel Alfonso noted at a weekly news briefing that Cuba's ambassador to Peru, Pedro Diaz, and the Cuban embassy counsellor, Jose Raul Silva, were among the hundreds of hostages at the residence.

"From the outset, the Cuban Foreign Ministry has followed this case with special attention. We have maintained contacts with Peruvian authorities and we have also had contacts with Japanese authorities," Alfonso said.

"We have been following this affair minute by minute," he said. "We have full confidence in the ability of the Peruvian authorities to manage this situation and we have confidence that a solution will be found."

In answer to questions, Alfonso said the ministry had no comment on any possible mediation by Cuba. Asked why Havana had stopped short of condemning the attack, he said Cuba's foreign policy was always guided by reason and silence could have its own value. He declined to elaborate.

The guerrillas are from MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement), said to be inspired by Cuba's revolution. This has led to speculation Havana might have some influence if it were called on to mediate.

The rebels -- holding about 400 people captive including high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and government officials -- have demanded the release of 400 to 500 jailed comrades and the presence of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori for talks.
